name: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
authors: Charles Packer, Sarah Wooders, Kevin Lin, Vivian Fang, Shishir G. Patil, Ion Stoica, Joseph E. Gonzalez (UC Berkeley)
venue: arXiv preprint (2023; v2 Feb 2024). Subsequently published as the LLM-OS/Letta line of work; the cited artifact is the arXiv:2310.08560 preprint.
code_url: https://research.memgpt.ai/ (code and data released; project later became the Letta/MemGPT open-source framework, https://github.com/letta-ai/letta)
reflection_type: none (in the self-critique/learning-from-failure sense). MemGPT is a memory-management / virtual-context system rather than a reflection method: the LLM self-directs reads/writes of its own memory tiers via function calls. The closest reflective behavior is that the conversational agent can 'remember, reflect, and evolve' by editing its working context, and a runtime feedback loop returns function execution results (including errors such as exceeding context capacity) so the agent can adjust subsequent memory actions. No learned critic, debate, or verifier is used.
feedback_source: self-generated (the LLM decides what to page in/out) plus system-level signals from the MemGPT runtime: memory-pressure / context-capacity warnings and function-call execution results / runtime errors (e.g. 'main context full'). For evaluation, an external GPT-4 LLM-judge and ground-truth gold answers are used to score outputs, but these are not fed back to drive the agent's behavior.
iteration_structure: iterative-refine within a task via function chaining: the LLM emits function calls that move data between main and external context, and can request an immediate follow-up inference (request_heartbeat=true) to chain multiple calls (e.g. paginated retrieval, multi-hop lookups) before yielding control. Event-triggered control flow (user messages, system warnings, timed events) drives inference cycles. No retry-with-reset, tree search, or population/evolutionary loop.
reflection_object: prompt/context — MemGPT modifies what occupies the LLM's own context window (working context block and FIFO queue) and external storage. The agent edits its in-context 'working context' (key facts, user preferences, persona) and pages historical messages/documents between context and external recall/archival storage, i.e. it reflects on and rewrites its own context/memory rather than its reasoning chain, output content, weights, or code.
requires_training: none — MemGPT requires no fine-tuning; it leverages off-the-shelf function-calling LLMs (GPT-4, GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-3.5 Turbo) purely via prompting and system scaffolding. (A separate later line, MemLLM, finetunes LLMs for explicit memory; MemGPT itself does not.)
reward_or_critic_model: none for the method itself (no reward model or trained critic drives memory operations). For evaluation only, a GPT-4 'LLM-judge' (self-as-judge style) scores DMR and document-QA answers for correctness.
distillation_target: episodic-memory / prompt. Information is distilled into (a) an in-context 'working context' text block (curated facts/preferences), (b) a recursive summary of evicted messages, and (c) external recall storage (conversation history) and archival storage (arbitrary-length text, e.g. documents, with vector search). These persist across sessions but are not distilled into reusable skills/workflows, structured rules, or model weights.
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered. The memory-management behavior is induced entirely by hand-written system instructions describing the memory hierarchy plus a function schema; it is an engineered OS-style scaffold, not an RL-emergent capability.
memory_type: long-term-episodic plus structured-notes. Two-tier hierarchy: main context (system instructions + fixed-size read/write 'working context' + FIFO message queue with a recursive summary at its head) and external context (recall storage = full message/event history; archival storage = read/write database of arbitrary-length text, e.g. 20M-article Wikipedia embeddings, backed by PostgreSQL + pgvector with an HNSW index).
memory_persistence: cross-session (production). Designed for long-term, multi-session conversational agents that remember and evolve across weeks/months; external recall and archival storage persist indefinitely beyond a single episode/session.
memory_curation_mechanism: self-summarized/curated + retrieval-gated + overwrite/evolution. A queue manager evicts FIFO messages on a memory-pressure warning (~70% context) and flush (~100%, evicting ~50%), regenerating a recursive summary of evicted messages; the LLM self-directs writes to working context and archival storage and can overwrite/update working-context facts. Out-of-context data is brought back only via explicit paginated search (retrieval-gated). This keeps the in-context footprint bounded while storing full history externally.
error_localization_granularity: holistic/outcome-level. MemGPT does not localize errors at step/token level; it operates at the level of whole memory operations and final answers. Runtime feedback flags coarse failures (e.g. context-capacity overflow), and evaluation is outcome-level (answer correct/incorrect).
intra_task_vs_inter_task: both. Intra-task: iterative function chaining/pagination to gather context within a single task (document QA, nested KV). Inter-task / cross-session: persistent memory carries facts and conversation history across sessions so the agent improves coherence over long-term interactions, though it transfers stored information rather than distilled task strategies.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mid-trajectory-recovery (in a limited, mechanical sense). The runtime feeds back function execution results and warnings (e.g. memory-pressure, capacity-exceeded errors) during a task so the agent corrects its memory-management actions in-flight (e.g. evicting/summarizing before overflow, continuing to search until a value is found in the nested-KV task). It is not failure-driven learning across episodes.
task_domains: dialogue (long-term multi-session conversational agents) and QA/reasoning over long documents (document analysis, multi-document QA, synthetic key-value retrieval). Broadly tool-use / decision-making via LLM function calling.
benchmarks: Multi-Session Chat (MSC) dataset (Xu et al. 2021), with an augmented MSC + new Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR) task and Conversation Opener task; document QA over a late-2018 Wikipedia dump (50 sampled questions, following Liu et al. 2023 'Lost in the Middle' retriever-reader setup); and a new nested Key-Value (KV) retrieval task (multi-hop lookups, 0-4 nesting levels, 140 UUID pairs ~8k tokens).
headline_result: On the Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR) consistency task, adding MemGPT raises GPT-4 accuracy from 32.1% to 92.5% (ROUGE-L recall 0.296->0.814) and GPT-4 Turbo from 35.3% to 93.4% (0.359->0.827); GPT-3.5 Turbo rises 38.7%->66.9% (0.394->0.629). MemGPT also sustains document-QA accuracy independent of context length and is the only method to solve nested-KV retrieval beyond 2 nesting levels (GPT-4/GPT-4 Turbo baselines hit 0% by 3 levels).
baselines: Fixed-context LLM baselines without MemGPT: GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613, 8k), GPT-4 Turbo (gpt-4-1106-preview, 128k), GPT-3.5 Turbo (gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, 16k). For chat, baselines see a lossy recursive summary of the prior five sessions; for document QA, baselines use the same top-K retriever (text-embedding-ada-002 cosine similarity) in a retriever-reader setup; truncation is also shown as a context-extension baseline in document QA.
gains_vs_baseline: DMR: +60.4 points accuracy for GPT-4 (32.1%->92.5%), +58.1 for GPT-4 Turbo (35.3%->93.4%), +28.2 for GPT-3.5 (38.7%->66.9%). Conversation opener: MemGPT matches/exceeds human-written openers (e.g. GPT-4 SIM-1 0.868 vs human 0.800). Document QA: MemGPT's accuracy is roughly flat as retrieved-document count grows while fixed-context baselines degrade (capped near retriever performance and hurt by truncation). Nested KV: MemGPT+GPT-4 stays near-constant across nesting levels whereas baselines collapse to 0% by 3 levels.
compute_cost_profile: Higher inference cost than a single forward pass: MemGPT issues multiple LLM inference cycles per task through function chaining/pagination (each memory read/write or paginated retrieval step is an additional LLM call), plus warning/summarization calls on context overflow. The paper does not report exact token/API-call multipliers or a quantified cost; trade-off is extra LLM calls and external storage (PostgreSQL/pgvector, HNSW index) in exchange for effectively unbounded context. No model training cost (no fine-tuning).
known_limitations: MemGPT depends on a sufficiently capable function-calling LLM: weaker models (GPT-3.5) underperform stronger ones with the same scaffold (e.g. GPT-3.5+MemGPT 66.9% vs GPT-4+MemGPT 92.5% on DMR; GPT-3.5 still drops off on nested KV). The agent sometimes stops paging through retriever results prematurely (early termination before exhausting candidates). The system relies on hand-engineered prompts/heuristics (memory-pressure thresholds, eviction policy, recursive summarization that is lossy). Evaluation is on a narrow set of tasks/domains (multi-session chat + document/KV retrieval) and uses an LLM-judge. No fine-tuning means behavior is bounded by base-model instruction-following.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: self-verify / external-tool. The agent's memory operations are self-directed with runtime tool feedback (function results, capacity warnings) but no ground-truth label is fed back to drive behavior. Evaluation correctness uses an LLM-judge plus gold answers (oracle for scoring only). It is not an intrinsic self-correction-of-reasoning method, so the Huang/Kamoi 'needs oracle' critique applies less directly; its gains come from retrieval/context management rather than label-guided self-correction.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent / net-positive for the memory-augmentation objective. MemGPT consistently and substantially improves the underlying base LLM on the targeted long-context tasks (large DMR and nested-KV gains). It is not a generic self-correction technique; its 'correction' is in-flight memory management (e.g. continuing to search, summarizing before overflow), which is reliably beneficial within these tasks but not evaluated as intrinsic answer self-revision.
calibration_effect: not-measured. The paper does not report calibration or confidence/overconfidence ('reasoning tax') metrics.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a — MemGPT is not a failure-attribution/diagnosis method; it neither classifies failure modes nor attributes responsible steps/agents.
failure_mode_addressed: Targets context-length / long-term-memory failure modes: forgetting facts across long multi-session conversations (loss of consistency/persona), inability to reason over documents exceeding the context window, and the 'lost in the middle' uneven-attention problem of long-context models. It mitigates premature termination of retrieval in the nested-KV setting via a 'keep searching until verified' persona. Not framed in terms of MAST's 14 multi-agent failure modes.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: Yes — released: an augmented MSC dataset with the new Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR) question/answer pairs and a session-6 consistency pair; a new nested Key-Value retrieval dataset; and a dataset of embeddings for ~20M Wikipedia articles, plus 50 sampled document-QA questions and all benchmark code at https://research.memgpt.ai.
builds_on: Toolformer (Schick et al. 2023) and LLM function-calling/tool-use; ReAct (Yao et al. 2022, reasoning+acting / 'plan out loud'); Generative Agents (Park et al. 2023, memory + LLM planner); WebGPT (Nakano et al. 2021, pagination to bound context); retrieval-augmented LMs (RAG, RETRO, In-Context RALM, REALM); long-context methods (Transformer-XL, Longformer, Positional Interpolation); 'Lost in the Middle' (Liu et al. 2023a) for the long-context failure motivation and KV task; AgentBench (Liu et al. 2023b); MSC dataset (Xu et al. 2021); OS virtual-memory paging concepts (Patterson et al.).
extended_by_or_inspired: Inspired a large line of LLM memory-OS and agent-memory systems, e.g. MemOS / MemOS: A Memory OS for AI System (Li et al. 2025), Mem0 (Chhikara et al. 2025), MemLLM (Modarressi et al., TMLR 2025), AIOS: LLM Agent Operating System (Mei et al.), MemOS for Memory-Augmented Generation, ENGRAM, Memori, VikingMem, CALMem, and 'The Missing Memory Hierarchy: Demand Paging for LLM Context Windows' (Mason 2026). The project itself evolved into the open-source Letta/MemGPT agent framework.
citation_count: 767 (Semantic Scholar, as of June 2026; Corpus ID 263909014)
reasoning_model_native: no — MemGPT was built and evaluated on standard instruction/function-calling LLMs (GPT-4, GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-3.5 Turbo), not on o1/R1-style models with built-in reflection. Its memory management is an external scaffold orthogonal to a model's native chain-of-thought; it could in principle wrap a reasoning model but the paper does not target one.
on_policy_distillation_link: Weak/indirect. MemGPT distills experience into external/episodic memory and curated context rather than into model weights or skills, so it is not an on-policy distillation or skill-optimization method; it relates to the broader 'distill experience into a reusable artifact' theme only via memory persistence, not weight/policy updates.
